display.title: Dry Bean
display.subtitle: Explore how bean morphology distinguishes seven dry bean varieties with a governed multiclass classification model.
display.problem_summary_title: Understanding dry bean morphology and multiclass classificat
display.problem_summary_body: This dataset examines how 16 numerical measurements of bean size and shape distinguish seven dry bean varieties. The task is multiclass classification: the model predicts one of seven classes and returns a probability distribution across all classes. Results describe predictive structure in the observed morphology data and should not be interpreted as causal or agronomic effects.

home_card.short_description: Classify dry bean varieties from 16 morphological measurements using a governed multiclass model that predicts one of seven bean classes and returns class probabilities.

documentation.content:
**Scientific study:** [dataset-study-dry-bean on GitHub](https://github.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean)  
**Dataset source:** [Dry Bean — UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/602/dry+bean+dataset)

This dataset presents a **multiclass-classification** problem based on numerical morphology measurements extracted from images of dry bean grains. The objective is to distinguish seven nominal bean varieties from 16 measurements describing size, dimensions, elongation, convexity, compactness, roundness, and related shape characteristics.

The analysis is predictive rather than causal. Morphological associations describe statistical structure in the observed sample; they do not establish causal or agronomic effects.

## Dataset overview

| Item | Value |
|---|---:|
| Bean samples | 13,611 |
| Source columns | 17 |
| Predictive features | 16 numerical features |
| Target | `Class` |
| Target classes | 7 |
| Problem type | Multiclass classification |
| Selected model | HistGradientBoostingClassifier |
| Selected feature policy | `all_features` |
| Primary model-selection metric | Macro F1 |
| Validation Macro F1 | 0.937881 |
| Final-test Macro F1 | **0.941835** |
| Final-test Balanced Accuracy | **0.939897** |

Each row represents one dry bean grain described by numerical morphology measurements already extracted from images.

The seven target classes are:

- `SEKER`
- `BARBUNYA`
- `BOMBAY`
- `CALI`
- `DERMASON`
- `HOROZ`
- `SIRA`

The target is nominal and unordered. There is no positive class and no binary decision threshold.

The predictive workflow starts after image feature extraction; it does not reproduce the original image-acquisition, segmentation, or measurement process.

## Analytical question

The analysis addresses two related questions:

1. **How do the observed morphology profiles differ among the seven bean varieties?**
2. **How effectively can those measurements classify previously unseen bean samples?**

The classifier uses the combined predictive information contained in the 16 numerical measurements and produces a probability distribution across all seven classes.

A final predicted class is obtained by selecting the class with the largest score or probability.

Observed relationships between a measurement and `Class` should not be interpreted as evidence that the measurement independently determines bean variety.

## Feature and target contract

The model uses the following numerical predictors:

```text
Area
Perimeter
MajorAxisLength
MinorAxisLength
AspectRatio
Eccentricity
ConvexArea
EquivDiameter
Extent
Solidity
Roundness
Compactness
ShapeFactor1
ShapeFactor2
ShapeFactor3
ShapeFactor4
```

The target column is:

```text
Class
```

`Class` is never used as a predictive input.

The source provides no observation identifier. Exact equality between feature profiles therefore cannot establish that two records represent the same physical grain.

## Data quality and preparation

The source contains 13,611 observations and 16 numerical candidate features.

Preparation preserves the source shape exactly:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Source rows | 13,611 |
| Prepared rows | 13,611 |
| Source columns | 17 |
| Prepared columns | 17 |
| Rows removed | 0 |
| Generic imputation | None |
| Automatic outlier deletion | None |
| Predictive features retained | 16 of 16 |
| Learned preprocessing during preparation | None |

The data is divided with a stratified **70% / 15% / 15%** split using random seed `42`:

| Partition | Rows | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Train | 9,527 | Cross-validation and model-family search |
| Validation | 2,042 | Frozen candidate comparison and selection |
| Final test | 2,042 | One-time holdout evaluation |

The final-test partition is kept sealed until all model-family, feature-policy, imbalance-policy, and hyperparameter decisions are frozen.

Repeated feature profiles are preserved. Because the source has no observation identifier, repeated-profile evidence does not prove duplicate identity or leakage.

## Class distribution

The seven classes have unequal support.

| Class | Rows | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `SEKER` | 2,027 | 14.89% |
| `BARBUNYA` | 1,322 | 9.71% |
| `BOMBAY` | 522 | 3.84% |
| `CALI` | 1,630 | 11.98% |
| `DERMASON` | 3,546 | 26.05% |
| `HOROZ` | 1,928 | 14.17% |
| `SIRA` | 2,636 | 19.37% |

`DERMASON` is the most frequent class and `BOMBAY` the least frequent. The majority/minority support ratio is approximately `6.79`.

![Dry Bean target class distribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/target_class_distribution.png)

Because support differs across classes, overall accuracy alone is not sufficient. Macro-averaged metrics give every class equal importance.

## Key exploratory findings

### Morphology contains strong class-related structure

Several morphology measurements show substantial univariate association with `Class`.

![Univariate feature-to-target associations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/feature_target_association_ranking.png)

The associations indicate predictive signal but are descriptive rather than causal.

### The feature space contains structural redundancy

Several numerical variables are strongly related, and some are mathematically derived from other measurements.

![Numerical feature correlation heatmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/numerical_feature_correlation_heatmap.png)

Nine derived dependencies are numerically confirmed:

```text
AspectRatio
Eccentricity
EquivDiameter
Solidity
Roundness
Compactness
ShapeFactor1
ShapeFactor3
ShapeFactor4
```

`ShapeFactor2` is handled separately. Its audited source formula is not numerically confirmed at the configured tolerance, so its provenance remains `unresolved`. This does not imply that the feature is invalid.

### Reduced-dimensional views show both separation and overlap

![Exploratory PCA class projection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/class_pca_projection.png)

The PCA projection is exploratory only. It shows meaningful class structure together with overlap among some varieties, but it is not itself a classifier and does not replace the full predictive feature space.

![Standardized class profiles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/standardized_class_profiles.png)

## Evaluation protocol

**Macro F1** is the primary model-selection metric because every class should contribute equally despite unequal support.

Complementary metrics include:

- Balanced Accuracy;
- Macro Recall;
- Weighted F1;
- overall Accuracy as contextual evidence;
- per-class precision, recall, and F1;
- multiclass Log Loss.

Candidate-family search uses training-only five-fold stratified cross-validation:

```text
StratifiedKFold
n_splits = 5
shuffle = True
random_state = 42
```

A candidate must exceed the Dummy validation Macro F1 by more than `0.02`.

A practical validation tie is defined as a Macro-F1 difference no greater than `0.002`.

When candidates fall inside that tolerance, predefined evidence is used to resolve the tie: Balanced Accuracy, worst-class recall, cross-validation stability, comparable Log Loss, simplicity, and stable model identity.

The final-test partition does not participate in selection.

## Model selection

The study uses a two-stage selection process.

First, four trainable model families are searched and ranked by training-only cross-validation. The two strongest families form the shortlist.

Second, the shortlisted families are evaluated under controlled feature-retention policies before final selection on the validation partition.

### Candidate-family comparison

| Model family | Search | Evaluated configurations | CV Macro F1 mean ± std | CV Balanced Accuracy | CV Weighted F1 | CV Log Loss ↓ | Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| HistGradientBoostingClassifier | RandomizedSearchCV | 8 of 64 | **0.937012 ± 0.003825** | **0.935424** | **0.924310** | 0.258114 | **Shortlisted** |
| LogisticRegression | GridSearchCV | 4 of 4 | 0.935031 ± 0.000996 | 0.933826 | 0.922071 | **0.218538** | **Shortlisted** |
| RandomForestClassifier | RandomizedSearchCV | 8 of 24 | 0.933343 ± 0.003635 | 0.931656 | 0.921274 | 0.342768 | Candidate |
| DecisionTreeClassifier | GridSearchCV | 8 of 8 | 0.919904 ± 0.009698 | 0.920557 | 0.908862 | 0.662884 | Candidate |

Decision Tree and Random Forest are not taken into the later validation-policy stage because they do not enter the CV-only shortlist.

### Candidate search configuration and hyperparameters

| Model | Search policy | Hyperparameters evaluated |
|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | GridSearchCV, 4/4 | `C={0.1,1.0}`; `class_weight={None,balanced}`; fixed `solver=lbfgs`, `max_iter=2000`, `random_state=42`; `StandardScaler` fitted within each fold |
| Decision Tree | GridSearchCV, 8/8 | `max_depth={8,None}`; `min_samples_leaf={1,5}`; `class_weight={None,balanced}`; fixed `random_state=42` |
| Random Forest | RandomizedSearchCV, 8/24 | `n_estimators={120,240}`; `max_depth={None,16}`; `min_samples_leaf={1,3}`; `class_weight={None,balanced,balanced_subsample}`; fixed `random_state=42` |
| HistGradientBoosting | RandomizedSearchCV, 8/64 | `learning_rate={0.05,0.1}`; `max_iter={150,250}`; `max_leaf_nodes={15,31}`; `min_samples_leaf={20,40}`; `l2_regularization={0.0,1.0}`; `class_weight={None,balanced}`; fixed `random_state=42` |
| Dummy prior | No search | `strategy=prior` |

The exact frozen configuration carried into final training is recorded for the selected model below. For non-selected families, the study's versioned evidence exposes the complete search contract and family-level CV results rather than a final production configuration.

### Feature-policy comparison

The two shortlisted families are evaluated using their frozen family-search parameters under three feature policies:

- all 16 features;
- all features except `ShapeFactor2`;
- seven features after removing the nine confirmed derived dependencies.

Validation results:

| Frozen candidate | Features | Macro F1 | Balanced Accuracy | Worst per-class recall | Log Loss ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HistGradientBoosting — all features | 16 | **0.937881** | **0.939131** | **0.870886** | 0.225172 |
| HistGradientBoosting — without ShapeFactor2 | 15 | 0.936677 | 0.938146 | 0.863291 | 0.229580 |
| Logistic Regression — all features | 16 | 0.928973 | 0.930908 | 0.863291 | **0.222511** |
| Logistic Regression — without ShapeFactor2 | 15 | 0.928917 | 0.930814 | 0.860759 | 0.223445 |
| HistGradientBoosting — without confirmed derived | 7 | 0.919956 | 0.920909 | 0.858586 | 0.278823 |
| Logistic Regression — without confirmed derived | 7 | 0.915406 | 0.914790 | 0.838384 | 0.271961 |

The Dummy validation Macro F1 is `0.059052`.

![Validation model comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/model_validation_comparison.png)

### Selected configuration

The selected candidate is:

```text
hist_gradient_boosting__all_features
```

| Hyperparameter | Selected value |
|---|---:|
| `class_weight` | `None` |
| `learning_rate` | 0.05 |
| `max_iter` | 250 |
| `max_leaf_nodes` | 15 |
| `min_samples_leaf` | 40 |
| `l2_regularization` | 0.0 |
| `random_state` | 42 |

All 16 numerical features are retained. No resampling is used.

## Feature-retention evidence

Removing `ShapeFactor2` from the selected family changes validation Macro F1 by approximately:

```text
-0.001204
```

The result measures predictive sensitivity only and does not resolve `ShapeFactor2` provenance.

Removing the nine confirmed derived features changes validation Macro F1 from approximately `0.937881` to `0.919956`, a delta of about:

```text
-0.017925
```

This evidence supports retaining all 16 features in the selected predictive configuration.

![Feature-policy sensitivity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/feature_policy_sensitivity.png)

## Final holdout evaluation

After every selection decision is frozen, the selected classifier is fitted once on train plus validation and evaluated once on the sealed final-test partition.

| Metric | Validation | Final test |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Macro F1** | 0.937881 | **0.941835** |
| Balanced Accuracy | 0.939131 | **0.939897** |
| Macro Recall | 0.939131 | **0.939897** |
| Weighted F1 | 0.926899 | **0.932187** |
| Accuracy | 0.927032 | **0.932419** |
| Log Loss ↓ | 0.225172 | **0.181024** |
| Minimum per-class recall | 0.870886 | **0.868687** |

The final test contains 2,042 previously unseen observations.

Macro F1 changes by approximately `+0.003954` from validation to test, while Balanced Accuracy changes by approximately `+0.000766`. These differences are descriptive generalization evidence and are not new selection gates.

`SIRA` has the lowest final-test recall.

![Final test confusion matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/final_test_confusion_matrix.png)

The two largest mutual confusion pairs are:

| Pair | Final-test mutual errors |
|---|---:|
| `DERMASON` ↔ `SIRA` | 58 |
| `BARBUNYA` ↔ `CALI` | 19 |

The residual errors are therefore concentrated more strongly among some morphologically overlapping varieties rather than being distributed uniformly.

![Validation vs test per-class recall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/validation_vs_test_per_class_recall.png)

![Validation vs test metrics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FabioAguiar/dataset-study-dry-bean/main/docs/images/validation_vs_test_metrics.png)

### Repeated-profile sensitivity

Fifteen final-test observations have a complete feature profile also observed in train plus validation.

Excluding those rows leaves 2,027 sensitivity observations:

| Evaluation | Macro F1 |
|---|---:|
| Official final test | 0.941835 |
| Sensitivity subset | 0.941523 |
| Delta | -0.000312 |

The official evaluation remains unchanged. This analysis does not establish duplicate identity or leakage.

## Understanding the main evaluation metrics

### Macro F1 — 0.941835

Macro F1 computes an F1 score independently for each class and then averages the seven class-level scores with equal weight.

This is appropriate because the class distribution is unequal and no variety should dominate the evaluation merely because it contains more observations.

**Higher values are better.**

### Balanced Accuracy — 0.939897

Balanced Accuracy averages recall across the seven classes.

It provides a direct view of whether the classifier maintains useful sensitivity across both frequent and infrequent classes.

**Higher values are better.**

### Accuracy — 0.932419

Accuracy is the overall proportion of correctly classified final-test observations.

Because each observation contributes equally, larger classes have more influence on this score than smaller classes. It should therefore be interpreted together with Macro F1 and Balanced Accuracy.

**Higher values are better.**

### Log Loss — 0.181024

Multiclass Log Loss evaluates the entire predicted probability distribution rather than only the final `argmax` class.

It penalizes confident probability assignments to incorrect classes and complements label-based metrics.

**Lower values are better.**

## Multiclass prediction and result interpretation

For each bean sample, the classifier produces a probability distribution across all seven classes.

The decision rule is:

```text
argmax
```

The class with the largest predicted probability is returned.

For example:

```text
SEKER      0.02
BARBUNYA   0.03
BOMBAY     0.01
CALI       0.86
DERMASON   0.02
HOROZ      0.04
SIRA       0.02
```

produces:

```text
CALI
```

No positive class or binary threshold is involved.

The full probability vector is more informative than the predicted class alone. A concentrated distribution indicates that one class is strongly preferred by the fitted model; similar probabilities among several classes indicate greater predictive ambiguity.

Probabilities are explicitly aligned to the official output class order:

```text
SEKER
BARBUNYA
BOMBAY
CALI
DERMASON
HOROZ
SIRA
```

These probabilities describe model support within the observed feature space. They are not guarantees of biological identity.

## What this study demonstrates

Dry Bean provides a technically rich example of tabular multiclass classification using numerical measurements derived from images.

It demonstrates:

- exploratory analysis of multiclass structure;
- unequal class support;
- deterministic data preparation;
- stratified train, validation, and final-test partitions;
- comparison of linear, tree, bagging, and gradient-boosting families;
- explicit hyperparameter-search spaces;
- a prior-only baseline;
- train-only cross-validation;
- controlled feature-retention experiments;
- multiclass Macro F1 and Balanced Accuracy;
- per-class diagnostics;
- sealed one-time final evaluation;
- probability-distribution output;
- explicit `argmax` class selection;
- residual confusion among morphologically overlapping classes;
- separation of predictive evidence from causal interpretation.

The study also illustrates why multiclass quality should not be summarized by accuracy alone. Macro F1, Balanced Accuracy, per-class recall, and Log Loss provide complementary views of the classifier's behavior.

## Limitations

- The evaluation uses a stratified random snapshot rather than temporal, prospective, or external validation.
- External representativeness is not established.
- Numerical image-derived measurements are evaluated, not the complete image-acquisition and feature-extraction process.
- Inference-time availability and stability of all 16 measurements are unconfirmed.
- `ShapeFactor2` source provenance remains unresolved at the configured numerical tolerance.
- Exact feature-profile equality cannot establish duplicate physical grains without source identifiers.
- Class probabilities are not established as universally calibrated measures of biological certainty.
- Morphological overlap remains between several classes.
- Distribution shift across equipment, environments, cultivars, populations, or acquisition protocols has not been evaluated.
- No production monitoring or drift policy is established.
- No application-specific cost model is included.
- Exploratory feature relationships do not establish causal or agronomic effects.
- Operational or industrial suitability is not established.

## Responsible interpretation

The evidence supports a clear predictive conclusion:

> Within this dataset and frozen evaluation protocol, numerical measurements of bean size and shape provide strong predictive information for distinguishing seven dry bean varieties. HistGradientBoostingClassifier using all 16 features achieves a final-test Macro F1 of approximately **0.9418** and Balanced Accuracy of approximately **0.9399**.

Four trainable model families are compared through training-only cross-validation. HistGradientBoostingClassifier and LogisticRegression form the shortlist, and controlled feature-policy evaluation supports retaining all 16 measurements before the final model is frozen.

The results demonstrate effective classification within the observed dataset. They do not establish causal morphology-to-variety relationships or guarantee the same performance for beans measured under different populations, equipment, environments, or acquisition procedures.

Use beyond this analytical setting would require representative external validation, verification of the complete measurement pipeline, assessment of probability behavior, evaluation under distribution shift, monitoring policies, and application-specific error costs.
